title: Mastering the Link Component
description: Go beyond basic linking: prefetching, scroll restoration, and passing refs to child components.

slides.title: The Link Component – Quick Recap 🔗
slides.content:
# Declarative Navigation

```jsx
import Link from 'next/link';

<Link href="/about">About</Link>
```

* Renders an `<a>` tag under the hood.
* Client‑side transition – no full page reload.
* **Prefetches** the linked page when it appears in the viewport (production only).

slides.title: Basic Link Usage (pages/index.js)
slides.content: Wrap any text or component to make it a navigational link.

quizData.question: When does Next.js Link prefetch a page?

options.text: When the link enters the viewport (in production)

quizData.explanation: In production, Link prefetches the page as soon as the link appears in the viewport, making transitions nearly instant. You can disable this with `prefetch={false}`.

slides.title: Advanced Props 🛠️
slides.content:
# Beyond href

* **`replace`** – replaces the current history entry instead of pushing a new one.
* **`scroll={false}`** – prevents scrolling to the top after navigation.
* **`prefetch={false}`** – disables automatic prefetching.
* **`passHref`** – forces the `href` to be passed to a child component (needed when wrapping custom components).
* **`legacyBehavior`** – for older Next.js patterns where you needed an `<a>` child.

slides.title: Link with Custom Component (passHref)
slides.content: If you wrap a custom component, you must forward the href.

quizData.question: Which prop prevents the page from scrolling to the top after navigating?
quizData.explanation: `scroll={false}` keeps the current scroll position. The default is `scroll={true}` which scrolls to top.

slides.title: External Links?
slides.content: For external URLs, use a regular `<a>` tag or the Link component with `target="_blank"`. Don't use Link for external unless you set `passHref` and handle it manually; a plain `<a>` is simpler.
